'''Paul Clifton Anthony George Sr.''' (born May 2, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''PG-13'''", he is a nine-time [[NBA All-Star]] and six-time member of the [[All-NBA Team]], as well as a four-time member of the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=20 Greatest Small Forwards Ever: The HoopsHype List |website=HoopsHype |date=2025-07-28
 |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/2025/07/28/20-greatest-small-forwards-ever-the-hoopshype-list/85410136007/ |access-date=2025-07-28
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=20 greatest defensive small forwards ever: The HoopsHype list |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rankings/2025/02/25/20-greatest-defensive-small-forwards-ever-the-hoopshype-list/79228509007/ |website=HoopsHype |date=2025-02-25 |publisher=HoopsHype |access-date=2025-06-25}}</ref>

George played high school basketball for [[Knight High School]] before playing two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State Bulldogs]]. He was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 10th overall pick of the [[2010 NBA draft]], and earned [[NBA All-Rookie|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors. He was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] in 2013, when he also earned his first All-Star selection and led the team to their first [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]] trip since 2004.

George suffered a broken leg in 2014 while competing for a roster spot on the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] for the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. He missed most of the 2014–15 season, but recovered to become an All-Star again in 2016, when he also won an [[Olympic Games|Olympic]] gold medal. He was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in 2017, and played two seasons for the Thunder before he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2019. The Clippers appeared in the playoffs four times during his tenure, including their first trip to the [[NBA conference finals|Conference Finals]] in 2021. George signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2024, where he played until he was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in 2026.

====2014–15 season: off-season injury====

===Philadelphia 76ers (2024–2026)===
====2024–25 season====
On July 6, 2024, George, then 34 years old, signed a four-year, $212 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/paul-george-2024-free-agency|title=Paul George signs 4-year max contract with 76ers|website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN NINE-TIME ALL-STAR AND SIX-TIME ALL-NBA SELECTION PAUL GEORGE|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-paul-george|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> With each of his previous jersey numbers, 24 and 13, retired by the franchise, George wore jersey number 8 as a tribute to Philadelphia native [[Kobe Bryant]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Paul George Reveals 76ers' No. 8 Jersey in Photos, Video; Honors 'Idol' Kobe Bryant|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10127462-paul-george-reveals-76ers-no-8-jersey-in-photos-video-honors-idol-kobe-bryant|website=BleacherReport.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}}</ref> The George signing gave the 76ers a star trio of George, center [[Joel Embiid]], and guard [[Tyrese Maxey]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42486989/sources-tyrese-maxey-challenged-joel-embiid-76ers-meeting|title=Sources: Maxey challenged Embiid over tardiness|date=November 19, 2024|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> The 76ers were expected to be contenders for the 2025 NBA championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44293744/76ers-paul-george-shut-rest-regular-season|title=76ers' George shut down for rest of season|date=March 17, 2025|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

George struggled with injuries and ineffectiveness in the 2024–2025 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thesixersense.com/latest-paul-george-update-could-foreshadow-a-dark-future-for-the-76ers-01jpk4s7jgsf|title=Latest Paul George update could foreshadow a dark future for the 76ers|date=March 17, 2025|website=The Sixer Sense}}</ref> He missed the first five games of the season after being diagnosed with a bone bruise from a hyperextended knee during the preseason.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=Paul George's Injury Report Status for 76ers-Suns Changes |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/paul-george-s-injury-report-status-for-76ers-suns-changes |access-date=2024-11-18 |website=Philadelphia 76ers On SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=Paul George returns from knee injury to make 76ers debut, scoring 15 points in loss to Suns |url=https://www.princegeorgecitizen.com/basketball/paul-george-returns-from-knee-injury-to-make-76ers-debut-scoring-15-points-in-loss-to-suns-9758448 |access-date=2024-11-18 |website=Prince George Citizen |language=en}}</ref> On November 4, 2024, he made his 76ers debut, putting up 15 points, five rebounds, and four assists in a 118–116 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/3-76ers-takeaways-paul-george-season-debut-vs-suns|title=3 76ers takeaways from Paul George's season debut vs. Suns|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=November 4, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}}</ref> On December 16, 2024, George put up 33 points, five rebounds, eight assists, two steals, and one block in a 121–108 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On December 28, 2024, against the [[Utah Jazz]], George surpassed [[Vince Carter]] for ninth in all-time three-pointers made with 2,291.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-paul-george-passes-vince-carter-on-all-time-3-point-shot-list|title=76ers' Paul George passes Vince Carter on all-time 3-point shot list|website=ClutchPoints|last=Breisch|first=Matty|date=December 28, 2024|access-date=December 29, 2024}}</ref>

On March 17, 2025, it was announced that George would miss the remainder of the season due to adductor and knee injuries. In 41 games, George averaged 16.2 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game. At the time the announcement was made, the 76ers had a 23–45 record.<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers' Paul George shut down for rest of regular season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44293744/76ers-paul-george-shut-rest-regular-season|access-date=March 19, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> George's season was described as "disappointing"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/sixers-news-analysis-paul-george-update-shut-down-nba-trade-rumors-stats-contract-highlights-lowlights-podcast-p/|title=What's next for Paul George and the Sixers after disappointing debut season?|date=March 18, 2025|website=PhillyVoice}}</ref> and "disastrous".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6212381/2025/03/18/paul-george-76ers-nba-draft-tank-unrivaled-wnba-nba-the-bounce/|title=Paul George's season-ending news means 76ers are tanking hard for NBA Draft|first=Zach|last=Harper|date=March 18, 2025|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref>
